message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 40 shares AAPL @ limit $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$8,916 total).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy within your mandate. The filing shows a business that is still growing modestly at scale with improving profitability: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), with Services up 13% to $96.2 billion and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income of $123.2 billion and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion. Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down from $97.0 billion / $6.13 only because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not an operating deterioration — a temporary, non-recurring item. The balance sheet remains very strong ($140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities, $97.3 billion of term debt) and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends. Risks I weighed include the 8% Greater China sales decline, flat iPhone revenue, and ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $222.90 — about 0.1% above the market, so close to current price — for roughly $8,916, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account.
